nativeValidation.setup: Use PowerShell at the root of a clean checkout containing the worker commit. Record the actual revision. On a volume and account that permit os.Root.Symlink, run the commands below. Copy the standalone Go CLI probe to its listed path after creating the validation directory. Run the denied commands in a separate session with a writable checkout and an account or volume where os.Root.Symlink is denied. Copy the same probe there.
deniedCommands: go run "$validationDir/verify-download-cli.go" "$validationDir/sandrun.exe" denied 2>&1 | Tee-Object "$validationDir/windows-denied-cli.log"; if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) { exit $LASTEXITCODE }
expectedResults: The directory symlink probe succeeds in the enabled session. The focused test, correction-failure test, traversal test and SandRun SDK suite pass.

The CLI build records the tested checkout revision with vcs.modified=false. The enabled CLI exits 0 and logs forward and backward cases with 2 files and 1 byte each, and the chain case with 7 writes and 3 bytes. All three preserve relative link text and return x through the link paths. The replacement is a regular file with xx and the dangling target stays missing.
The injected correction failure removes link, warns with its path and counts the one remaining file and byte.

Under denial, the os.Root.Symlink probe reports failure, the denied test and CLI exit 0, dir/file.txt remains readable with x, link is absent and the result reports 1 file, 1 byte and 'link: the symbolic link could not be created'.
